Regulation: B.C. Reg. 113/2026
Made under: Provincial Sales Tax Act
Published in: No. 13 – B.C. Regs. 110 to 124, July 14, 2026
Deposit date: July 9, 2026

B.C. Reg. 113/2026, deposited July 9, 2026, under thePROVINCIAL SALES TAX ACT[sections 236 and 241]. Order in Council 293/2026, approved and ordered July 9, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, (a)	effective October 1, 2026, the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation, B.C. Reg. 97/2013, is amended as set out in the attached Appendix 1, and (b)	effective June 1, 2027, the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation is amended as set out in the attached Appendix 2. — B. BAILEY,Minister of Finance; A. DIX,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 11 of the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation, B.C. Reg. 97/2013, is repealed. 2	Section 73 (1) is amended by striking out "A related service provided" and substituting "Subject to section 73.1, a related service provided". 3	The following section is added: Exception – clothing and footwear 73.1(1)	In this section, a reference to clothing or footwear does not include clothing or footwear that would be exempt under Division 8[Safety Equipment and Apparel]of Part 2. (a)	section 73 (1) (b), to the extent the tangible personal property is clothing or footwear that would be exempt under section 9 (2) or (3)[children’s clothing and footwear]or 10[used clothing and footwear], and does not apply in respect of any consideration for a provision of a related service in relation to clothing and footwear that (c)	becomes due on or after October 1, 2026, and (d)	has not been paid before October 1, 2026. 4	Section 77 (2) is amended by adding the following paragraph: (e.1)	dry-cleaning, wet-cleaning and laundry services;. minutes_briefs.title: PST exemption ends for dry-cleaning, laundry, and related services on clothing and footwear in BC
minutes_briefs.summary: British Columbia is removing the Provincial Sales Tax (PST) exemption for certain services. Starting October 1, 2026, PST will apply to related services (like alterations or repairs) performed on clothing and footwear, unless the item itself is already exempt (e.g., children's clothing or used items). Starting June 1, 2027, PST will also apply to dry-cleaning, wet-cleaning, and laundry services. This means businesses providing these services must start charging PST on those dates.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Update your billing systems to charge PST on clothing/footwear related services from October 1, 2026, and on dry-cleaning/laundry services from June 1, 2027.

key_dates.label: PST on clothing/footwear related services takes effect (BC)
PST on dry-cleaning and laundry services takes effect (BC)
